content:
I asked Claude to write an environment linter that, for every to_additive-declaration, checks that both or neither carry a doc-string. Running it over Mathlib surfaced a few hundred cases (somewhat surprisingly, flagging some missing multiplicative doc-strings!).

I then asked Claude to fill in the missing documentation, which was mostly straightforward, since there was already one witness to additivise/multiplicativise.

Claude then opened 10 PRs, to spread the review cost, I looked at all of them, had a couple of iterations and they are ready. I will post them below, one per message to help the bots.
• #41636 — Algebra/Group actions & homs
• #41637 — Algebra/Group core & sub-objects
• #41638 — MeasureTheory.Measure
• #41639 — MeasureTheory.Group
• #41640 — GroupTheory.GroupAction
• #41641 — GroupTheory (misc)
• #41642 — Topology / Geometry / Analysis
• #41643 — category theory
• #41644 — Algebra (BigOperators, Order, …)
• #41645 — Combinatorics / Dynamics
As a personal reflection: getting Claude to fix the linter issues was much more pleasant than doing it by hand! :slight_smile:
@Damiano Testa Nice! Will you also PR the actual linter that found these gaps?

I am still thinking about a good design for the linter: I would like the linter to be a syntax linter, rather than an environment linter, but sometimes, the attribute or the docstring is added after the declaration (e.g. for classes/defs/aliases). In those cases, the linter would have to be silenced.

In fact, another consequence of this experiment is that I think that to_additive may also be extended to take care of adding the doc-strings to alias, to_fun, irreducible_def and the various cross-references (stacks, kerodon, wikidata, lmfdb).
#41565 removes many superfluous uses of add_decl_doc (and is not exhaustive at that).
If we fix all of them, would the syntax linter then have no false positives?

I think that right now alias is the biggest source of linter exceptions. An aliased declaration gets an auto-generated doc-string, saying that it is the alias of something else. But if the alias is not applied to the additive version, then the additive declaration does not get the doc-string.
Actually, the syntax linter may not pick that up and you would not have "exceptions", but I would consider that to be a bug in the linter, rather than a success.
I recently fixed the interaction between to_additive and alias in terms of this docstring. Are you on a recent enough mathlib? (#40503)
Ah, I may not be! Although my memory is that there were far more missing to_additive alias docstrings, so maybe what is missing is being thorough in using the feature.
Jovan, in terms of detection, would it make sense for to_additive itself to perform this check?
Yes, I think so

After having proposed this, I also thought that if someone uses alias on a declaration that has to_additive translate, flagging the other is not really a to_additive job, so a linter should exist anyway and it might as well take care of the whole job.
Wait, are you suggesting a linter for missing to_additive tags? That sounds very different from a linter for missing docstrings on to_additive declarations.

I've already seen two false positives in review (both stating there is a more general version of the multiplicative lemma with no additive counterpart)
So a linter would not be 100%

Damiano Testa said:

I asked Claude to write an environment linter that, for every to_additive-declaration, checks that both or neither carry a doc-string.

I thought we already had this in Lean 3!
Regarding the linter itself; this could alternatively be part of the implementation of to_additive
That won't helpw with add_decl_doc, but would work fine for direct docstrings

Jovan Gerbscheid said:

Wait, are you suggesting a linter for missing to_additive tags? That sounds very different from a linter for missing docstrings on to_additive declarations.

I was not, but a consequence of maintaining a weak pairing between pairs of to_additive-related declarations does create a version of "missing to_additive.

This combined with the fact that I believe that adding a doc-string to an aliased to_additive declaration happened on a version of mathlib that was more recent than the one I used for my experiment, so it looked like a more widespread phenomenon than it really was.

Anyway, this whole discussion is making me believe that maybe we _should_ have a linter that looks for missing to_additive tags and then, checking for docstrings is something that could be implemented easily either by the same mechanism or by to_additive.
If we had a "perfect application" of to_additive, I suspect that the false positives would disappear as well.
